speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe the appearance of the lesion on your left dorsal hand, including its color, shape, and any scaling or crusting?

speaker: Patient
text: 65-year-old female. The patient is here for an annual well-check. She has a history of well-controlled diabetes and hypertension, managed with metformin and losartan, respectively. She reports maintaining a healthy diet primarily consisting of vegetables and lean meat, denies any tobacco or alcohol use, and enjoys outdoor activities like walking and sunbathing.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that background; given your sun exposure, has this lesion been present for a long time, and does it tend to bleed or crust easily if touched? Also, do you notice any pain, itching, or burning sensations associated with it?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is The presence of a rough, scaly, sandpaper-like plaque on the left dorsal hand. I also have No tenderness, No pain. To keep my notes clear, please give only one final answer and keep it to a single direct conclusion.

speaker: Doctor
text: REQUEST TEST: Skin Biopsy of the left dorsal hand lesion. REQUEST IMAGES: Close-up clinical photograph of the lesion.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Skin Biopsy findings show hyperkeratosis with parakeratosis, solar elastosis, and atypical keratinocytes confined to the epidermis, consistent with actinic keratosis.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Actinic Keratosis on the left dorsal hand.
